actions.description: Drive a mobile base with a commanded linear and angular velocity for a bounded duration, or to a target pose. Obstacle and zone limits are enforced by the binding safety envelope.

inputs.description: Commanded yaw rate before the upstream Navigation clamp
inputs.name: angular_velocity

inputs.name: duration_s

actions.name: drive

actions.description: Command both wheel targets to zero through Navigation.move_wheels. The upstream exposes no wheel-velocity readback and no deceleration profile, so the receipt reports that the zero command was applied, not that the simulated base was measured at rest.

facts.text: ADAM is the ADAMSim robot class; its constructor connects a PyBullet GUI client and loads the robot URDF with the requested fixed-base flag.
The ADAM constructor defaults use_realtime, use_fixed_base and use_ros to True.
The ADAM constructor sets the control period self.t to 0.01.
The ADAM constructor creates the Sensors and ArmsKinematics modules and creates Navigation only when use_fixed_base is false.
The ADAM constructor imports and constructs ROSConnection only when use_ros is true.
ADAM.step calls p.stepSimulation() only when use_realtime is false, measures the execution speed, and then sleeps for self.t or delegates to the ROS rate.

Navigation.send_velocity clamps the linear and angular velocity to self.linear_speed and self.angular_speed, converts them to left/right wheel velocities with the wheel radius and wheel distance, and applies PyBullet VELOCITY_CONTROL to both wheel joints.
Navigation.move_wheels applies PyBullet VELOCITY_CONTROL to both wheel joints with the given left and right wheel speeds and force.
Navigation.move_base_continuous commands both wheel targets to zero with force 10 when its target is reached.
The Navigation constructor sets wheel_radius 0.0762, wheel_distance 0.436, linear_speed 6.55 and angular_speed 1.0.
Sensors.get_camera_angle returns the camera joint position converted to degrees minus 45.
ArmsKinematics.get_arm_joint_angles reads the arm joint angles in radians from PyBullet.
semantic_groups_inspire_hands.json lists six joints for the right arm and six for the left arm.
The README describes ADAMSim as a PyBullet-based simulation environment for the ADAM domestic mobile manipulator, with navigation, arm and hand kinematics, perception and ROS communication.
The README requires ROS 1 Noetic and Python 3.8 and says ADAMSim is developed for Ubuntu/Linux.
The navigation example constructs ADAM with use_fixed_base=False and use_ros=False.
The navigation loop calls move_base_continuous and then advances the simulation with adam.step() in the same iteration.
The ADAM constructor calls p.setRealTimeSimulation(1) when use_realtime is true and p.setRealTimeSimulation(0) otherwise.
The ADAM constructor stores the real-time flag as self.use_realtime and the ROS flag as self.use_ros.
When the robot_info JSON file is missing, the ADAM constructor generates it with print_robot_info(save=True).
ROSConnection.sleep reads self.adam.useRealTimeSimulation to choose between rospy.sleep(self.adam.t) and self.rate.sleep().

The ROSConnection constructor initialises the ROS node adam_ros_node, subscribes /robot/left_arm/joint_states and /robot/right_arm/joint_states, creates JointTrajectory publishers on /robot/left_arm/scaled_pos_traj_controller/command and /robot/right_arm/scaled_pos_traj_controller/command and a Twist publisher on /robot/move_base/cmd_vel, and starts a 0.02 s hand-service timer and a 1/120 s real_to_sim timer.
ROSConnection.real_to_sim moves the simulated arms and hands to the latest arm joint states and hand states received from the robot.
ROSConnection.call_get_angle_act calls rospy.wait_for_service on /robot/<arm>/inspire_hand/get_angle_act with no timeout before calling the service.
The README says the architecture allows synchronized operation between the real robot and its digital twin, including experiments running both simulated and real robots simultaneously.

determinism.notes: The fake integrates the commanded velocity with a fixed 0.01 s period and no physics solver, contacts, actuator model or wall-clock pacing; placeholder state does not establish a trajectory or state-hash replay.

gaps: the fake is a pure-Python kinematic stand-in for the ADAM base: it runs no PyBullet, no rigid-body dynamics, no contacts, no wheel friction and no GUI, and it is not a recording of captured simulator traffic
one fake tick is 10 ms, the ADAM control period self.t (scripts/adam.py:77); the PyBullet physics timestep is not set by ADAM and is not modelled or claimed by the fake

the native backend is not declared: constructing the real simulator needs pybullet, a PyBullet GUI client (scripts/adam.py:51), ROS 1 Noetic and Python 3.8 (Readme.md:39), and it was neither installed nor run by this package

the arms are read-only state: no arm or hand command is exposed because the upstream has no arm stop, arm quiescence feedback or gripper stop, and the camera, lidar and RGB-D outputs are not exposed (NOT COVERED in RESULT.json)
the fake's wheel radius, wheel distance, linear/angular clamp and 10 ms period are the upstream constructor values copied to mirror Navigation.send_velocity and ADAM.step, not device limits
the zero-velocity stop is a motor-target command: the clone has no wheel-velocity readback, so the safe-state action cannot prove that the simulated base reached zero speed

the ADAM constructor defaults are use_fixed_base=True and use_ros=True (scripts/adam.py:21-31): with a fixed base it creates no Navigation (:97-98), so drive, stop and e-stop need use_fixed_base=False; with use_ros, ADAM.step calls ROSConnection.sleep, which reads self.adam.useRealTimeSimulation (scripts/ros_connection.py:64), an attribute ADAM never assigns (it stores use_realtime, scripts/adam.py:74), so every step fails at the pin

in PyBullet real-time mode (use_realtime, the ADAM default; scripts/adam.py:54) the world advances by itself and ADAM.step only sleeps, so ending the step calls does not stop it; in stepped mode each ADAM.step is one stepSimulation at a PyBullet timestep ADAM does not set, so the dead-reckoned distance (applied velocity times duration_s) is not the simulated travel

constructing ADAM opens a PyBullet GUI client, prints to stdout, writes the robot_info JSON into the clone's config directory when it is missing (scripts/adam.py:51, :81-83), and with use_ros initialises a ROS node whose timers mirror the real robot's arms into the simulation and block in rospy.wait_for_service on the real hands' services (scripts/ros_connection.py:14-37, :159-196)

safe_state.description: Both wheel targets are commanded to zero through Navigation.move_wheels (PyBullet VELOCITY_CONTROL, force 100) and the driver stops calling ADAM.step: in real-time mode (use_realtime, the ADAM default) the world keeps advancing and the wheel motors brake toward zero, in stepped mode it stays frozen until the next ADAM.step applies the zero targets, and with no wheel-velocity getter this is a commanded stop, not measured quiescence; the arms are not commanded.
